gen-gf-autour-one-gf-aclonica: Stretched wide and deep through the middle of each lowercase letter, the plain sans body has a shift in stroke you feel more than see. Aclonica would carry a long page easily, while Autour One keeps its round, expressive letters up top.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-allerta: Allerta spreads its letters wide and loose, with a prominent x-height that makes the plain sans lines easy to scan. Allerta sits beneath Autour One's bold, expressive heading like a quiet room after a loud entrance.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-alumni-sans: Autour One draws its bold curves like vinyl cut to a single line width. Alumni Sans does the opposite job, with a wide-open c and a soft, brush-pressed thick-thin shift that suits steady reading.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-alumni-sans-pinstri: Chunky heading, tall lowercase body. Alumni Sans Pinstripe sets towering small letters beside tiny capitals in a tight word texture, so if Autour One were shrunk down, its bold presence would fade quickly.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Wire-bent heading, squeezed-in body. Alumni Sans SC lets its oversized lowercase run tightly packed, with stems just barely heavier than the hairlines, so extended text reads as a dense, contemporary texture beneath Autour One.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-anaheim: Round, bold, and thin-looking all at once, Autour One gets paired with a body of dense, modern letters. Anaheim fills the line with lowercase that rivals capitals, so a modest body size is enough against that heading.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-arsenal: Hairlines never appear in Autour One; every curve stays solid, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. And Arsenal, with its x-height close to cap height, reads as a close-knit, mildly stressed line over many paragraphs.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-arsenal-sc: Autour One has no stress in any curve, which gives its bold shapes an unusual flatness. Arsenal SC then smooths the reading pace with mild thick-thin differences and a tight fit between characters over a long passage.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-asimovian: Asimovian builds tall lowercase from a single stroke width, giving the sans-serif body a stacked, upright look. Asimovian and Autour One both avoid fuss, the heading round and bold, the body narrow and approachable.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-basic: Expressive and bold, Autour One traces every letter with a line of constant weight and barely any cap-to-lowercase step. Basic, in contrast, rises gently from small letters to capitals, so shrinking the heading would leave it faint.
